{
  "status": "NEEDS_IMPROVEMENT",
  "SYSTEM_INTERPRETATION_OF_USER_INTENT": "The system appears to interpret past purchases as continuing interest in broad product families or musical styles, with insufficient attention to the specific reason for the next choice.",
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_RIGHT": [
    "Recommendations align when they support a concrete activity or add a useful capability to equipment users already own.",
    "Music recommendations align when they capture a specific combination of sound, artist affinity, and recurring listening interests."
  ],
  "WHERE_THE_SYSTEM_GETS_IT_WRONG": [
    "Broad category connections repeatedly produce suggestions for unrelated tasks, device uses, or musical experiences.",
    "Prior ownership is treated as continuing demand, producing redundant devices, duplicate supplies, and unjustified quantities.",
    "Older or occasional interests carry into recommendations despite stronger evidence of a more specific recent preference."
  ],
  "OVERUSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Shared category, brand ecosystem, or broad genre is treated as sufficient evidence of relevance.",
    "Surface similarities such as assortment size, compilation format, or artist familiarity substitute for a concrete reason to choose."
  ],
  "UNDERUSED_OR_MISSED_DECISION_PATTERNS": [
    "Repeated recent behavior provides a stronger indication of current purpose than isolated historical purchases.",
    "Compatibility, dimensions, usable quantity, and capabilities already owned determine whether related products are useful additions.",
    "Specific combinations of musical qualities, themes, and seasonal context matter more than broad stylistic overlap.",
    "When item identity or history is insufficiently informative, inferred relevance remains uncertain rather than establishing a choice-worthy match."
  ],
  "PRIMARY_FAILURE_MODE_AT_TOP_OF_LIST": "Top recommendations too often share a broad association with past behavior without satisfying the concrete purpose, compatibility, or current preference needed to motivate a choice.",
  "DIAGNOSTIC_SIGNALS_TO_TRACK": [
    "The share of top-ranked recommendations users would choose, grouped by category and whether item identity is sufficiently known.",
    "The frequency of top-ranked rejections attributed to unrelated purpose, incompatible specifications, redundant ownership, or excessive quantity.",
    "The frequency with which broad historical matches outrank items users prefer for their specific recent interests."
  ]
}
